newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude steady, more Minas trades into China.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude steady, more Minas trades into China.

text.p: Asian crude prices were steady on Wednesday as another cargo of Minas was heard traded into China.
Market sources said the March crude was traded at ICP -10 cents but there were still barrels available. Assessments on Minas values ranged from ICP flat to ICP -50 cents.
Traders said there was still Minas available on the market, but that 600,000 to 800,000 barrels of Duri were also overhanging the market.
Another 600,000 barrels of Duri was in floating storage pending the restart next week of the Balongan refinery.
That might lead to a weak April market as Pertamina looks to filter the overhanging Minas and Duri into the market. However, China's buying appetite would be critical.

The 38-day maintenance shut down of the Dumai refinery and problems at Balongan have hit Minas and Duri -- the main feedstock for those refineries -- pushing both crudes to trade around ICP -50 cents.
The backwardation on the Dubai market was narrowing, in line with the weakness seen on Brent and WTI, although backwardation on Tapis remained strong at 70 cents, brokers said.
The more active May/June Dubai was quoted 15/23 cents from 18/25 a day-earlier and 18/23 in New York.
A producer had reduced its April asking price for Tapis to around 95 cents, which traders assessed as slightly above the market of 75/85 cents.
Traders said a European major sold a cargo of March 23-25 Tapis to a Thai refinery. The deal was being kept P+C and traders had heard prices for the deal talked between quotes +60 cents and +$1.00.
In addition, they said there was a complicated structure to the deal. --Singapore Newsroom (+65 870 3081)
